title: Artificial Intelligence Lifecycle
audience: Basic science learners studying AI project planning
objectives: Walk through the major lifecycle decisions in a molecular AI classification project.
Practice choosing data sources, preprocessing steps, models, and validation methods.
Connect each lifecycle decision to bias, rigor, and generalizability.

sections.name: Collecting Molecular Data
sections.purpose: Choose an appropriate data source and reflect on possible bias.
sections.how_to_use: Select a source such as ChEMBL, PubChem, in-house data, or simulated molecules, then write why it fits the project.

sections.name: Preprocessing and Feature Engineering
sections.purpose: Identify what must happen before raw molecular data can be modeled.
sections.how_to_use: Select cleaning, standardization, descriptor generation, missing-data handling, scaling, and labeling steps.

sections.name: Model Selection
sections.purpose: Compare model choices for molecular classification.
sections.how_to_use: Choose a model and explain why its assumptions fit molecular fingerprints and the project goal.

sections.name: Model Validation
sections.purpose: Plan how to test model generalizability.
sections.how_to_use: Select validation approaches such as cross-validation, external testing, or scaffold-aware holdout validation.

chatbot_guidance: When asked how to use this notebook, guide the learner through the four lifecycle steps in order.
For basic science users, emphasize data provenance, molecular representation, validation design, and generalizability.
